standards.name: FAANG Sample Metadata Specification
standards.abstract: This specification defines metadata for biological samples used in FAANG projects, covering donor animals, tissue specimens, primary cells, cell cultures, pooled specimens and derived samples. Records are intended to be registered in EMBL-EBI BioSamples and use ontology terms where appropriate; data take the form of structured sample attributes (text, dates, numbers, ontology terms, URLs, references to other samples and protocols). The document is maintained by the FAANG Data Coordination Centre (FAANG DCC) and references EMBL-EBI BioSamples as the required archive; it lists required, recommended and optional attributes for different sample material types and gives data-type and unit constraints.

classification.rationale: The source presents a concrete metadata specification as a list of named attributes with explicit data types (e.g. 'Sample name (text)', 'Organism (NCBI taxon ID)', 'specimen collection date (date)'). This is a field-level table-like structure (required/recommended/optional attributes) rather than prose guidance or a process DAG.

standards.name: FAANG Experiment Metadata Specification
standards.abstract: This specification defines metadata for experiments performed under the Functional Annotation of Animal Genomes (FAANG) project. It covers experiments on biological specimens (organisms, cell samples, cell cultures) and records metadata about sequencing or array assays; recording modalities include sequence read archive submissions and array experiment records. The standard is maintained by the FAANG metadata group (repository: FAANG/faang-metadata) and is intended to harmonize required, recommended and optional attributes for experiment records submitted to public archives (ENA/NCBI/DDBJ, ArrayExpress, GEO). It addresses what fields must be present for common experiment types (e.g. ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, Bisulfite sequencing, Hi-C, RNA-seq), provides data types for each attribute, and gives controlled-value lists or ontology guidance where applicable.

classification.rationale: The source presents a concrete list of named attributes with explicit data types (e.g. 'sample (BioSample ID)', 'assay type (ontology term)', 'sampling to preparation interval (number)'), including enumerated possible values for many fields. This is a field-level metadata table rather than a prose checklist or ordered workflow.

standards.name: FAANG Analysis Metadata Specification
standards.abstract: This specification covers metadata for computational analyses performed on raw experimental data (e.g., sequencing reads from ChIP-seq) and the derived analysis results (alignments, QC metrics, peak calls, normalized signal plots). Published and maintained by the FAANG (Functional Annotation of Animal Genomes) metadata/DCC group, the document defines required process- and QC-level attributes to make analyses reproducible and discoverable, gives concrete data types for key fields, and provides file-naming conventions and recommendations for sharing analysis code and containers.

classification.rationale: The source presents explicit attribute names together with data types (e.g. "total reads (number)" and "mapped reads (number)") and structured fields such as 'Input data', 'Reference data', and subfields of 'Analysis protocol'. This is a field-level specification rather than prose guidance or an ordered workflow, so it matches the TABLE form.

file_name.name: file_name
file_name.descr: Human-readable unique file name composed of ordered components separated by dots (dots within fields replaced by underscores); includes a data-freeze date and file format.
file_name.evidence:
Each file should be uniquely identifiable with a human readable name, giving sufficient information to understand what it contains. We expect analysis to be repeated at intervals, as reference data and protocols are updated, so a data freeze date is included.

Short names based on the following, separated with a dot (‘.’):
• species / assembly version
• sample name
• sample description (tissue or cell type)
• assay type
• experiment target
• experiment ID
• analysis protocol name
• results type (e.g. genotypes vs. sites for 1000genomes vcf files)
• data freeze date
• file format

The dots existing in any field will be replaced by underscore ('_'), e.g. OAR3_1 for OAR3.1

standards.name: FAANG Data Type Definitions
standards.abstract: This document defines the expected data types for attributes submitted to the FAANG project via the EBI BioSamples system. It covers common attribute value modalities such as dates (ISO 8601), ontology term references (e.g. NCBI Taxonomy or UBERON terms), numeric values with units, URLs/protocol links, free-text fields, location expressed as a set of three attributes (name, latitude, longitude), and references to samples (by name or BioSample ID). The guidance is published by the FAANG Data Coordination Centre (FAANG DCC) and is intended to ensure consistent format and semantic linking (via 'Term Source' and 'Term Source ID') when submitting sample metadata to BioSamples.

classification.rationale: The source lists named metadata attribute types (date, NCBI taxon ID, number, protocol, text, URL, ontology term, location, sample) and gives an explicit expected data format for each. This is a field-level specification (a metadata table) rather than prose guidance or a stepwise workflow.

date.name: date
date.descr: Date values must be reported using ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD for dates or YYYY-MM for months); the format must be reported as the 'units'.
date.evidence: Dates should be reported in an [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format,  YYYY-MM-DD for dates or YYYY-MM for months. To ensure clarity, the format must be reported as the 'units'.

raw_full_info.raw: date: Dates should be reported in an ISO 8601 format, YYYY-MM-DD for dates or YYYY-MM for months. To ensure clarity, the format must be reported as the 'units'.

NCBI_taxon_ID.name: NCBI taxon ID
NCBI_taxon_ID.descr: Species name and identifier from the NCBI Taxonomy; record the term value as the species name, term source as 'NCBI Taxonomy' and term source ID as the numeric taxonomy ID (e.g. 9606).
NCBI_taxon_ID.evidence: A species name and identifier from the [NCBI Taxonomy database](http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/taxonomy). For example, [human](http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/taxonomy/9606) would be described in the term with value of 'Homo sapiens', term source as 'NCBI Taxonomy' and term source ID as 9606.

raw_full_info.raw: NCBI taxon ID: A species name and identifier from the NCBI Taxonomy database. For example, human would be described in the term with value of 'Homo sapiens', term source as 'NCBI Taxonomy' and term source ID as 9606.

number.name: number
number.descr: Numeric value with units; units should be given without abbreviations. Use units from the Unit Ontology (UO) where appropriate.
number.evidence: A number, with units specified. BioSamples recommends that units are given without abbreviations. Terms defined in the [UO](http://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/uo) are encouraged to be used. For example, a birth weight could have a value of 1.3 and the units specified as '[kilogram](http://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/uo/terms?short_form=UO_0000009)' .

raw_full_info.raw: number: A number, with units specified. BioSamples recommends that units are given without abbreviations. Terms defined in the UO are encouraged to be used.

ontology_term.name: ontology term
ontology_term.descr: Reference to an ontology term: attribute value should be the term label; include the ontology (term source) and the term source ID (ontology identifier).
ontology_term.evidence: A reference to an ontology term. The attribute value should be the term label. The term source should be the ontology used, and the term source ID should be an ID from that ontology. For example, cerebral cortex could be  described with an ontology term from 'UBERON' with ontology ID of 'UBERON:0000956' and the attribute value is 'cerebral cortex'. Though in the experiment submission, direct links to ontologies cannot be submitted as attributes. The use of ontology terms is still encouraged by setting the attribute value to exactly match the term name in the ontology.

standards.name: FAANG JSON‑Schema Validation Rulesets
standards.abstract: These rulesets define JSON‑Schema validation rules for metadata submitted to the FAANG data coordination centre. They cover metadata describing biological samples, experiments (assays such as RNA‑seq, ChIP‑seq, ATAC‑seq), and downstream analyses; recorded as JSON objects and validated with the FAANG metadata validation library. The files are maintained alongside the FAANG DCC metadata repository on GitHub and split into core rules and module-specific rules (including legacy variants) to specify required fields, types, enumerations and constraints for submission and downstream use.

classification.rationale: The source material is a collection of JSON‑Schema files that present explicit named properties with concrete types, enums and structural constraints (i.e. a genuine metadata table mapping field names to types and allowed values).
